title: Electrical Monitoring and Multi-Signal Telemetry
summary: Correlate synthetic power, service, network, cooling, and maintenance signals.
objectives: Combine voltage, current, load, UPS, generator, alarm, and environmental evidence.
Separate direct observations from inferred causes and identify safe handoffs.

vocab.def: Recorded measurements or states used to understand a modeled system.
A relationship between observed signals that does not by itself prove causation.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: All signals are synthetic. Do not troubleshoot energized systems or change thresholds in production.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Compare a power alarm, server alert, network device state, cooling warning, and recent maintenance note. Ask which signals share a time window or dependency, then identify what remains uncertain.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Create a concise handoff with timestamps, affected domain, evidence, prohibited actions, and escalation owner.

practice.prompt: Does a power alarm alone prove the root cause of a service outage?
practice.answer: No. Correlate the available signals and preserve uncertainty.

quiz.question: What is correlation?
options: A relationship that does not alone prove causation
quiz.answer: A relationship that does not alone prove causation

reflectionPrompt: Which signal was direct evidence and which was an inference?
